flags.why: Ô means a city gateway, short for cửa ô, rather than a quarter outside the citadel ([dictionary](https://thuviensach.vn/img/pdf/6762-tu-dieng-tieng-viet-thuviensach.vn.pdf)).
flags.fix: city gate; gateway (especially those of old Hanoi)

flags.why: The speaker asks permission to ask for directions, rather than asking the listener to ask for directions.
flags.fix: Excuse me, may I ask you for directions?

flags.why: Lừa bóng is ordinary current football vocabulary, so rare is misleading ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-l%E1%BB%ABa)).
Bận meaning an occasion or time also occurs in ordinary speech and is not restricted to literary language ([dictionary](https://vtudien.com/viet-viet/dictionary/nghia-cua-tu-b%E1%BA%ADn)).
A ca used for measuring has variable capacity, rather than necessarily holding about a quarter litre ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/ca#Tiếng_Việt)).
flags.fix: mugful; a measure equal to the contents of a measuring mug

flags.why: The example explains the letter name instead of using it in context.
flags.fix: Em viết chữ ca vào ô đầu tiên. = Write the letter K in the first box.

flags.why: Ca is not a Vietnamese preposition meaning at or in, and the purported archaic construction is invalid ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/ca#Tiếng_Việt)).
Ca does not have the claimed Vietnamese meaning place ([dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/ca#Tiếng_Việt)).
The entry omits the very common use of Tây to refer to a Western person.
